rubric.filler: a hesitation or self-repair sound ('ee', 'hmm', 'eh' before a restart or while searching), a backchannel hum, or 'apa namanya' while searching: removable without losing meaning or tone
rubric.not_filler: a filler-lexicon token with a meaning: an interjection addressing someone or expressing surprise, a quoted interjection, a tag question ('..., eh?'), a word cut short
rubric.particle: a protected discourse particle (plan §7.3): never listed
rubric.reduplication: both words of a reduplicated word ('hati hati', 'bener -bener'): never listed
rubric.emphatic: a deliberate repetition ('iya, iya', 'sorry, sorry, sorry'): never listed
rubric.stutter: the earlier occurrence(s) of a restarted word or phrase: removable
rubric.not_repeat: the same word twice with different roles or across a sentence end
rubric.borderline: a reasonable editor could decide the other way; counted as labelled, and reported both ways

method: Samples are consecutive words (±6 around the labelled tokens, merged when they overlap) with the audio-timeline silences and laughter spans around them. Label groups: W every detector filler item in the ±60 s editor windows of the 26 clips of the five real jobs; H a deterministic random sample (seed 20260928) of 40 detector filler items outside those windows, plus every filler hit in their context; R the detector's repeat items in the windows and repeats found by scanning every immediate token repeat there; D reduplication pairs (hyphen-split ones in the windows, and unhyphenated pairs of the lexicon in the whole transcripts); P protected particles, each at least once and in repeated or filler contexts; S the synthetic job's Rapikan sentences (scripts/editor_fixture/make_job.py, clip 2); A an authored sentence for 'lho', which occurs in no source (Whisper writes 'loh'). Labels were decided by the agent (T3.5) from the surrounding words; every filler hit inside a sample carries a label, so precision covers every hit. The owner confirms the labels at checkpoint 3.
